Form D name match only: Bing Gordon is a director on Zume's 2018-10 $375M SoftBank filing, but Crunchbase News on that round names him only as a former EA executive who 'joined Kleiner Perkins as a partner in 2008' and does not say a KP fund invested; the firm's own site never listed Zume, no filing names a KP vehicle and The Robot Report's Series B story names no investor. A vendor profile puts Kleiner Perkins in the $48M Series B (2017-10), which no press or filing read confirms, so the seat is not corroborated as fund money (decisions.md D3).

Homonym: Weili Zhou, a director of a Raleigh, North Carolina biotech that sold $50,000 in 2018, is not Kleiner Perkins' Wei Zhou and signs at the company's address; no KP fund is named.

Partner's personal angel check (decisions.md D3): Yardbarker's 2008 round lists 'Russ Siegelman (who invested personally, not as part of his firm, Kleiner Perkins)' (VentureBeat, 2008-04-03); his 2009 Form D seat is at a personal Palo Alto address and no KP fund is named.

SPAC shell (T5; JUDGE-BRIEF membership trap): Thayer Ventures Acquisition Corp is the listed shell that merged with Inspirato in February 2022; the KP filings on it report Inspirato stock the firm held from its private rounds, and Inspirato is its own member row.

Unmanned Innovation, Inc. is Airware ('incorporated as Unmanned Innovation, Inc.', Wikipedia), which the firm listed on kpcb.com 2014-2018 (Digital team, Mike Abbott); Mike Abbott signs the 2014-07-15 Form D from 2750 Sand Hill Road, and AgFunderNews names KPCB as lead of that $25M Series B. Duplicate of the base row airware.

note: Airware, the commercial drone operating system (San Francisco from 2014). Kleiner Perkins entered at the $25M Series B: 'The round was lead by Kleiner Perkins Caufield and Byers, with Andreessen Horowitz and First Round Ventures also contributing' (AgFunderNews, 2014-07-24); the Series A was a16z's and GV's, so the band's Series A is disputed. Ceased operations 2018-09-14 (TechCrunch) and Delair bought its assets (Wikipedia; The Drone Girl, 2019-03-11): acquired with a successor note, as the airware row and the a16z, Felicis and GV books read it. Same company as the base row airware.

basis: V Vehicle Co is Next Autoworks under its earlier name, which the firm listed on its 2012 company pages (Greentech team, Ray Lane); both 2009 Forms D name Ray Lane and John Doerr as directors 'c/o KPCB Holdings Inc, 2750 Sand Hill Road'. Duplicate of the base row next-autoworks.

note: San Diego car startup (V-Vehicle, renamed Next Autoworks), backed by Kleiner Perkins with T. Boone Pickens and Google Ventures. Ray Lane and John Doerr were already directors on the June 2009 bridge filing, so Kleiner Perkins entered at that round or earlier (the company filed a paper Form D in 2007); no source names the round, so the stage is undetermined. The DOE refused its loan in November 2011 and it closed its headquarters in December 2011 with no later activity: defunct, as GV's next-autoworks row reads. Same company as the base row next-autoworks.

WebMD Corp /NEW/ is Healtheon (CIK 1009575: Healtheon Corp to 2000, WebMD Corp /NEW/ to 2005, then Emdeon Corp and HLTH Corp). Healtheon's 1999 prospectus: 'On January 26, 1996, Healtheon sold 10,285,000 shares of its Series A preferred stock for $.50 per share', purchasers including Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VII and KPCB VII Founders Fund; KPCB VII also bought the October 1996 Series B. HQ Elmwood Park, NJ (the 2004 13G/A's issuer address). HLTH merged into WebMD Health Corp in 2009, which Internet Brands (KKR) bought in 2017: acquired. Same company as the base row healtheon.

Visioneer, the PaperPort desktop scanner maker founded March 1992 (Wikipedia). Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VI and KPCB VI Founders Fund reported ceasing to hold over 5% of its common stock on the 1998-02 13G/A (issuer business address Fremont, CA). The IPO prospectus is not on EDGAR (the company's filings start 1996-05) and no source read names the round the fund entered: undetermined. Visioneer bought ScanSoft from Xerox and took its name in 1999, became Nuance in 2005, and Microsoft acquired Nuance in 2022: acquired stands.
